graph_equivalence.conclusion: B2 and B3 present the SAME compute graph: identical architecture, identical frozen shapes, identical trainable parameter names, shapes and count, and identical optimizer construction. They differ ONLY in the values of frozen weights. Training throughput is a function of shapes and operations, not of values, and this forward has no data-dependent control flow, so B2 is a valid throughput proxy for B3. This static argument is confirmed empirically below rather than trusted on its own.

additionally_verified_20260807.why: the conclusion ASSERTED both. Both are true, but asserting is not verifying, so both are now checked in code and recorded. A value-dependent branch would have to test tensor CONTENTS, which is what the tokens above look for.

empirical_equivalence.scale: train_40k, the cheaper scale, so the pretrained identity pays as little as possible to confirm the proxy
empirical_equivalence.criterion: the difference in mean step time is within three standard errors OF THE DIFFERENCE. An earlier version compared it against three standard deviations of a single step, which is about fifteen times looser and would have accepted a genuine five per cent throughput gap. Recomputed here from the recorded per-step statistics; no new GPU work was needed, because the criterion is a function of numbers already measured.
empirical_equivalence.verdict: CONFIRMED under the STRICTER criterion: B2 and B3 train at the same rate, so B2 validly calibrates B3's throughput

same_scale_bias_correction.why: a steady-state step window is not an epoch. The real training loop also pays the scheduler step, the wall check and a per-step host synchronisation on the loss, and it pays the epoch's first and last steps at cold rates. Extrapolating steps to epochs therefore UNDER-predicts, and by how much can be measured at 40k, where twelve real full-epoch train times exist.
same_scale_bias_correction.basis_used_in_the_budget: the P90 step time extrapolated and then corrected by the same-scale P90 bias, which is the conservative combination
same_scale_bias_correction.consequence: the CORRECTED 250k rate is at or slightly ABOVE the step-scaled assumption it replaced, not below it. An earlier version of this record concluded the assumption was CONSERVATIVE; that conclusion came from comparing an UNCORRECTED extrapolation against the assumption and was WRONG.

against_the_assumption.verdict: after the same-scale bias correction the measured rate is ABOVE the step-scaled assumption: the assumption was OPTIMISTIC, not conservative. Comparing the UNCORRECTED extrapolation against it would have said the opposite, and did in an earlier version of this record.
